newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish, Greek foreign ministers hold talks.
newsitem.headline: Turkish, Greek foreign ministers hold talks.

text.p: Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller began talks with her Greek opposite number Theodoros Pangalos on Wednesday, a day after Greece announced it would maintain its veto on European Union aid to Turkey.
The two ministers met on the sidelines of a meeting at the Black Sea Economic Cooperation (BSEC) forum in Istanbul.
They made no comment to reporters before the meeting.
On Tuesday, Pangalos said at a meeting of EU ministers in Luxembourg that Greece could not agree to unblock aid worth 375 million ecus ($424 million) over a dispute with Turkey in the Aegean.
"We have repeatedly declared that we cannot accept Turkish behaviour vis-a-vis our sovereignty," he told a news conference.
The veto dashed hopes of other EU members Athens would ease its stance against its rival. Ciller said the move was disappointing.
The aide has been promised to help Ankara meet the increased competition posed by the customs union with the EU which took effect in January 1996.
Despite the veto, EU officials reported some progress at the Luxembourg meeting.
Greece and Turkey formally agreed an approach to solving differences in the Aegean, where they almost came to war last year over some uninhabited islets.
Pangalos was scheduled to leave Turkey on Wednesday evening.
